title: Failed/retried transaction post-incumbent kill sweep
purpose: Test explicit recent transaction failures after an incumbent route already exists: repeated equipment failure after repair, repeated procurement attempts, cross-city testing workarounds and failed acceptance. Retain only a low-permission post-incumbent edge that mature diagnostic/procurement/third-party routes still cannot handle.
scan_rule: SECOND/THIRD PROCUREMENT != MISSING SUPPLY by default
CROSS-CITY OUTSOURCING != LOCAL ROUTING FAILURE when third-party service + logistics already works
A retry is useful only if the failure cause itself maps to a narrow post-incumbent edge that Rooter can own without becoming prime contractor, maintenance manager or qualification shell.

patterns_tested.pattern: Repeated equipment failure after warranty/OEM repair
patterns_tested.named_event: Xuzhou heavy-vehicle manufacturing dust-system VFD board failure
observed_failure: The VFD had already failed twice.
Warranty/manufacturer repair restored the circuit board.
Line and motor insulation were normal, but the reason for repeated board burning was not identified.
The buyer reopened procurement for on-site cause diagnosis, corrective measures and a six-month non-recurrence commitment.
patterns_tested.connection_pressure: STRONG / BUYER IS ACTIVELY REPURCHASING AN OUTCOME
incumbent_counterevidence: Domestic equipment-health providers already sell 24x365 remote diagnosis, on-site diagnosis for complex faults, root-cause reports, repair verification and predictive-maintenance services.
Equipment-hospital/maintenance platforms already offer mechanical/electrical fault diagnosis, dispatch, repair management and repair-quality acceptance.
The buyer's own inquiry channel already allows an outcome-level service package to be purchased.
patterns_tested.missing_edge: NO DISTINCT NEUTRAL ROUTING EDGE OBSERVED
patterns_tested.rooter_risk: Would become expert broker or maintenance-management layer with high bypass after the buyer finds a competent RCA provider.

patterns_tested.pattern: Annual outsourced maintenance but recurring environmental electrical faults
patterns_tested.named_event: Four machining centers at a Xuzhou manufacturing site
observed_failure: Equipment has ongoing annual outsourced maintenance.
Welding smoke and metal dust continue entering electrical cabinets because there is no physical isolation.
Regular electrical cleaning did not eliminate repeated electrical faults or uptime loss.
The buyer is again outsourcing a targeted electrical-maintenance package.
incumbent_counterevidence: Current condition-monitoring and predictive-maintenance providers already sell environmental/electrical/mechanical diagnosis, root-cause analysis, maintenance recommendations and closed-loop verification.
The failure points toward scope/engineering correction, not absence of a provider-routing market.

observed_events: Xuzhou telecom equipment-repair DICT project republished a second time with a small budget but substantial qualification/safety requirements.
Several Xuzhou telecom system-integration/digitalization projects reached third procurement after insufficient responders or only one bidder passed review.
Military/equipment projects also show third-round purchasing.
counterevidence: Visible failures frequently arise from minimum-valid-bidder rules, qualification requirements, competition rules or formal procurement governance.
Current procurement systems explicitly define re-tender/direct-purchase transitions when valid responses are below thresholds.
patterns_tested.missing_edge: PROCUREMENT-GOVERNANCE FAILURE, NOT A PROVEN COUNTERPART ROUTING GAP
patterns_tested.rooter_risk: Any attempted fix would trend toward prime contracting, qualification-shell behavior or tender agency rather than low-permission routing.

patterns_tested.pattern: Local capability absent, test outsourced to another city
patterns_tested.search_target: A named Xuzhou private manufacturer repeatedly forced to send one specific test to Nanjing/Suzhou/Shanghai with measurable time/cost after current shared-testing/third-party routes are considered.
counterevidence: Xuzhou public quality-testing procurements already award capable providers in Nanjing, Suzhou, Qingdao and Shanghai, showing cross-city delegation is an established transaction route.
Third-party testing procurement can bundle sample collection/aggregation/logistics when local capability is absent.
Shared-lab precedents elsewhere materially reduce prior cross-city testing cost and report lead time, showing the mechanism is institutionally solvable rather than an unserved generic route.

patterns_tested.pattern: Current production-stoppage-sensitive repair tasks with explicit lead-time/stop-time questions
observed_events: Blasting-elevator top roller shaft wear: buyer asks supplier to state material lead time, repair period and whether/how long production must stop.
Main-transformer GIS chamber low pressure: buyer similarly asks repair duration/material lead time/production-stop impact.
Industrial robot repair is actively procured.
patterns_tested.meaning: These prove naturally occurring urgent service demand and measurable time sensitivity.
patterns_tested.counterevidence: The tasks already enter direct procurement/repair channels; urgency alone does not establish a missing routing edge.

material_learning: Repeated failure is a stronger search signal than trend evidence, but still not sufficient.
Outcome failure after repair can create demand for independent RCA, yet mature RCA/condition-monitoring markets already exist.
Repeated procurement can be created by governance/qualification mechanics rather than missing suppliers.
Cross-city service can be a functioning route rather than evidence of local market failure.

The next useful search should target informal/manual workarounds actors repeatedly perform outside formal channels because the formal transaction unit is too slow, too large, too bureaucratic or unavailable.
cross_industry_result.current_best_next_truth: Fresh Scan 016 should search current Xuzhou/Jiangsu private-actor behavior for repeated informal/manual workarounds such as owners/employees personally transporting parts/samples, borrowing tools/capacity, calling acquaintances, using WeChat groups or splitting tasks manually because formal channels do not fit the required time/unit. Require a recent event and measurable cost before retaining anything.
